question: Which royal favorite am I?
reference: Esther 3-7 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Haman')

clues: The king promoted me above all his other officials and ordered everyone to bow to me.
One man at the palace gate refused, and it filled me with rage.
I cast lots to pick the day to wipe out his entire people.
I was impaled on the very stake I had set up for that man.

question: Which betrayer am I?
reference: Matthew 26-27; John 12 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Judas No. 4', p. 129)

clues: I kept the money box for the group, and I used to help myself to what was put in it.
I complained loudly when a woman poured expensive perfume over Jesus.
I agreed to hand him over for thirty pieces of silver.
I marked him out with a kiss, then flung the money into the temple and hanged myself.

question: Which seamstress disciple am I?
reference: Acts 9:36-42 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Dorcas')

clues: I lived in Joppa and was always doing good deeds and giving to the poor.
I sewed robes and other garments for the widows of the congregation.
When I fell sick and died, they laid me in an upstairs room and sent two men to fetch Peter.
He put everyone out of the room, prayed, and said, "Tabitha, rise!"

question: Which tentmaker am I?
reference: Acts 18:1-3, 24-26 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Aquila')

clues: My wife and I were Jews forced to leave Rome when the emperor expelled all the Jews.
We settled in Corinth and worked at our trade, making tents.
The apostle Paul stayed with us and worked alongside us.
Later, in Ephesus, my wife and I took the eloquent Apollos aside and explained the way of God to him more accurately.

question: Which runaway slave am I?
reference: Philemon 10-18 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Onesimus')

clues: I ran away from my master, who was a Christian, and somehow ended up with Paul in prison.
Paul became like a father to me there.
Paul sent me back carrying a personal letter that appealed for my welcome.
My name means "useful," and Paul made a point of the fact that I had become just that.

question: Which slave-owner am I?
reference: Philemon 1-19 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Philemon, Letter to')

clues: A congregation met in my house.
Paul wrote me a short, warm, personal letter.
He urged me to take back a runaway slave, no longer as a slave but as a brother.
He offered to pay whatever the man owed me, and reminded me that I owed him my very self.

question: Which Greek companion of Paul am I?
reference: Galatians 2:3; 2 Corinthians 7; Titus 1:5 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Titus No. 1')

clues: I was a Greek, and Paul refused to have me circumcised as a test case for the nations.
Paul sent me to Corinth to deal with a painful situation, and I came back with encouraging news.
Paul later left me on the island of Crete to appoint elders in city after city.
A whole letter of the Christian Scriptures is addressed to me.

question: Which physician and historian am I?
reference: Colossians 4:14; Luke 1:1-4; Acts 1:1; 2 Timothy 4:11 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Luke')

clues: Paul called me the beloved physician.
I wrote an orderly account of Jesus' life for a man named Theophilus, then a sequel about the apostles.
In parts of that sequel the account shifts to "we," because I was traveling with Paul.
From his final imprisonment Paul wrote that only I was still with him.

question: Which Gospel writer who once turned back am I?
reference: Acts 12:12; 13:13; 15:37-39; 2 Timothy 4:11 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Mark, John')

clues: My mother's house in Jerusalem was a meeting place for the disciples.
I set out with Paul and Barnabas but left them partway through and went home.
Paul refused to take me on the next trip, and he and Barnabas split over it.
Years later Paul asked for me by name, saying I was useful to him for ministering.

question: Which disciple sent to a persecutor am I?
reference: Acts 9:10-19; 22:12 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Ananias No. 2')

clues: I lived in Damascus and was well spoken of by the Jews there.
In a vision the Lord told me to go to a house on the street called Straight.
I protested, because the man waiting there had come to arrest people like me.
I laid my hands on him, something like scales fell from his eyes, and I baptized him.

question: Which prophet who acted out his message am I?
reference: Acts 11:27-28; 21:10-11 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Agabus')

clues: I came down from Judea to Antioch and foretold a great famine over the whole inhabited earth.
Years later I met Paul at Caesarea.
I took Paul's belt, bound my own hands and feet with it, and said the Jews would bind its owner this way in Jerusalem.
Paul went up to the city anyway.

question: Which official on a desert road am I?
reference: Acts 8:26-39 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Ethiopian Eunuch')

clues: I was a court official in charge of the treasury of the queen of Ethiopia.
I had gone to Jerusalem to worship, and was riding home reading aloud from the scroll of Isaiah.
A man ran up and asked whether I understood what I was reading, and I invited him into my chariot.
When we came to some water, I asked to be baptized right there.

question: Which mother in old age am I?
reference: Luke 1:5-25, 39-45, 57-63 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Elizabeth')

clues: My husband was a priest, and I too was descended from Aaron.
I was well past childbearing age when I conceived.
When my young relative Mary came to visit, the baby leaped inside me and I was filled with holy spirit.
I insisted my son be named John, though no one in the family had that name.

question: Which grudge-holding queen am I?
reference: Mark 6:17-28 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Herodias')

clues: I left my first husband to marry his brother, a district ruler.
A wilderness preacher publicly condemned the marriage, and I wanted him dead.
At my husband's birthday feast, my daughter danced and delighted him and his guests.
I told her to ask for the preacher's head on a platter.

question: Which man pressed into service am I?
reference: Mark 15:21; Luke 23:26 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Simon No. 8')

clues: I was coming in from the countryside just as a condemned man was being led out to die.
Roman soldiers seized me and forced me to carry his torture stake.
I was the father of Alexander and Rufus, men the early Christians knew.
I walked behind him to the place called Skull.

question: Which carpenter am I?
reference: Matthew 1:18-25; 2:13-15; Luke 2:41-48 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Joseph No. 7')

clues: I was engaged to a young woman who was found to be pregnant before we came together.
An angel told me in a dream to take her as my wife anyway.
After the child was born, another dream warned me to flee with them to Egypt.
The last time the Bible mentions me, the boy is twelve and we are anxiously searching for him in Jerusalem.
